REGIONAL REGULATION OF SAROLANGUN REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2023

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF SAROLANGUN,

Considering : a. that women and children are assets of the nation who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from violence and discrimination in order to build society, nation and state; b. that as violence against women and children in Sarolangun Regency increases, which is an act that degrades human dignity and worth, the role of the Sarolangun Regency government is needed so that women and children are protected from violations of rights guaranteed by the Constitution; c. that based on the considerations referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women and Children; In View Of : 1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1999 Number 165, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3886); 3. Number 54 of 1999 concerning the Establishment of Sarolangun Regency, Tebo Regency, Muaro Jambi Regency and East Tanjung Jabung Regency (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2000 Number 81, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3969); 4. Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2002 Number 109, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4235), as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606); 5. Article 13

(1) Protection of women includes:

a. social protection;
b. economic protection; and
c. legal protection.
(2) Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection to ensure the fulfillment of decent living needs.
(3) Economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is to prevent and address vulnerability risks resulting from shocks and social vulnerability of a person, family, group and/or community for the survival of women.
(4) Legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented in terms of providing protection to women who become witnesses and victims of violence and discrimination.

Article 3

The regulation regarding Empowerment and Protection of Women and Children aims to:

a. ensure the fulfillment of the rights of every woman and child to survival, growth and development;
b. improve the quality of life of women, children and the quality of families; c. enhance the institutional capacity of women's empowerment and child protection in the region, including the development of gender and child data systems; and
d. provide protection of women's rights and fulfillment of children's rights including special protection for children from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment.

Article 30

(1) Women and children victims of violence who require continuous treatment have the right to stay in a safe house.

(2) The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) provides a temporary safe place or shelter for victims of violence until their rights are restored.

(3) The administration and management of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the regional apparatus that performs functions inthe field of women's and children's empowerment.

(4) Further provisions regarding the administration of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 7

(1) Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the empowerment and protection of women.

(2) Efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. determination of policies, programs, and activities to improve the quality of life of women related to development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture;
b. provision of services to women especially to victims of violence, female workers, elderly women, and women with disabilities, conflict victims and disaster victims; and
c. implementation of gender mainstreaming in government institutions, women's study centers, research and development institutions, non-governmental institutions.
(3) Efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
(4) Empowerment and protection of women is coordinated by Regional Apparatus that administers regional government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sarolangun Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional People's Representative Council according to the principles of autonomy and co-administration with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that constitute the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent is the Regent of Sarolangun.
5. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the organizer of Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of the social and cultural conditions of society.
10. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
11. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
16. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
17. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (narcotics) abuse, child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect.
19. Safe house is a shelter or temporary protection house for victims during the assistance process to ensure the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators and is only known to interested parties for the safety and security of victims.
20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community, business world, and media commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sarolangun Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional People's Representative Council according to the principles of autonomy and co-administration with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that constitute the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent is the Regent of Sarolangun.
5. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the organizer of Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of the social and cultural conditions of society.
10. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
11. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
16. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
17. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (narcotics) abuse, child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect.
19. Safe house is a shelter or temporary protection house for victims during the assistance process to ensure the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators and is only known to interested parties for the safety and security of victims.
20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community, business world, and media commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.

Article 3

The regulation regarding Empowerment and Protection of Women and Children aims to:

a. ensure the fulfillment of the rights of every woman and child to survival, growth and development;
b. improve the quality of life of women, children and the quality of families; c. enhance the institutional capacity of women's empowerment and child protection in the region, including the development of gender and child data systems; and
d. provide protection of women's rights and fulfillment of children's rights including special protection for children from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment.

Part Three

Protection of Women

CHAPTER II

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sarolangun Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional People's Representative Council according to the principles of autonomy and co-administration with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that constitute the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent is the Regent of Sarolangun.
5. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the organizer of Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of the social and cultural conditions of society.
10. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
11. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
16. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
17. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (narcotics) abuse, child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect.
19. Safe house is a shelter or temporary protection house for victims during the assistance process to ensure the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators and is only known to interested parties for the safety and security of victims.
20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community, business world, and media commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.

Article 32

(1) The Regent carries out guidance and supervision of the administration of women's empowerment and child protection in the Region. (2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Regional Apparatus in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs.

(3) The Regional Apparatus in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs as referred to in paragraph (2) is the coordinator of the implementation of the administration of women's empowerment and child protection in the Region.

Article 13

(1) Protection of women includes:

a. social protection;
b. economic protection; and
c. legal protection.
(2) Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection to ensure the fulfillment of decent living needs.
(3) Economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is to prevent and address vulnerability risks resulting from shocks and social vulnerability of a person, family, group and/or community for the survival of women.
(4) Legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented in terms of providing protection to women who become witnesses and victims of violence and discrimination.

8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of the social and cultural conditions of society.

16. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.

18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (narcotics) abuse, child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect.

20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community, business world, and media commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.

IMPLEMENTATION OF EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF SAROLANGUN,

Article 7

(1) Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the empowerment and protection of women.

(2) Efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. determination of policies, programs, and activities to improve the quality of life of women related to development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture;
b. provision of services to women especially to victims of violence, female workers, elderly women, and women with disabilities, conflict victims and disaster victims; and
c. implementation of gender mainstreaming in government institutions, women's study centers, research and development institutions, non-governmental institutions.
(3) Efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
(4) Empowerment and protection of women is coordinated by Regional Apparatus that administers regional government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 3

The regulation regarding Empowerment and Protection of Women and Children aims to:

a. ensure the fulfillment of the rights of every woman and child to survival, growth and development;
b. improve the quality of life of women, children and the quality of families; c. enhance the institutional capacity of women's empowerment and child protection in the region, including the development of gender and child data systems; and
d. provide protection of women's rights and fulfillment of children's rights including special protection for children from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sarolangun Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional People's Representative Council according to the principles of autonomy and co-administration with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that constitute the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent is the Regent of Sarolangun.
5. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the organizer of Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of the social and cultural conditions of society.
10. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
11. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
16. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
17. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (narcotics) abuse, child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect.
19. Safe house is a shelter or temporary protection house for victims during the assistance process to ensure the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators and is only known to interested parties for the safety and security of victims.
20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community, business world, and media commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.

Article 29

The Regional Government endeavors to fulfill the Right to Special Protection for children by:

a. developing programs to prevent children from being involved in the situations and conditions as referred to in Article 27 paragraph (3);
b. providing access to public services and social security for children with disabilities; and
c. providing 24 (twenty-four) hour complaint service facilities, Shelters,rehabilitation centers and orphanages.

Article 30

(1) Women and children victims of violence who require continuous treatment have the right to stay in a safe house.

(2) The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) provides a temporary safe place or shelter for victims of violence until their rights are restored.

(3) The administration and management of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the regional apparatus that performs functions inthe field of women's and children's empowerment.

(4) Further provisions regarding the administration of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Part Three

Protection of Women

Article 13

(1) Protection of women includes:

a. social protection;
b. economic protection; and
c. legal protection.
(2) Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection to ensure the fulfillment of decent living needs.
(3) Economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is to prevent and address vulnerability risks resulting from shocks and social vulnerability of a person, family, group and/or community for the survival of women.
(4) Legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented in terms of providing protection to women who become witnesses and victims of violence and discrimination.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sarolangun Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional People's Representative Council according to the principles of autonomy and co-administration with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that constitute the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent is the Regent of Sarolangun.
5. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the organizer of Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of the social and cultural conditions of society.
10. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
11. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
16. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
17. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (narcotics) abuse, child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect.
19. Safe house is a shelter or temporary protection house for victims during the assistance process to ensure the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators and is only known to interested parties for the safety and security of victims.
20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community, business world, and media commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.

7. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of the social and cultural conditions of society.
10. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
11. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
16. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
17. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (narcotics) abuse, child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect.
19. Safe house is a shelter or temporary protection house for victims during the assistance process to ensure the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators and is only known to interested parties for the safety and security of victims.
20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community, business world, and media commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.

Article 13

b. economic protection; and
c. legal protection.

Article 6

(1) Every wife during the marriage bond has the same rights and responsibilities as her husband over all matters relating to her marital life, relationship with her children, and ownership and management of joint property in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Women's empowerment in the economic field as referred to in Article 8 letter a is implemented through:

e. facilitation of marketing network development.

Article 32

(1) The Regent carries out guidance and supervision of the administration of women's empowerment and child protection in the Region. (2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Regional Apparatus in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs.

(1) Financing for the administration of women's empowerment and child protection is sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget. (2) In addition to being sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, financing for the administration of women's empowerment and child protection may be sourced from other legitimate and non-binding financing sources.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sarolangun Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional People's Representative Council according to the principles of autonomy and co-administration with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that constitute the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent is the Regent of Sarolangun.
5. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the organizer of Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of the social and cultural conditions of society.
10. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
11. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
16. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
17. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (narcotics) abuse, child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect.
19. Safe house is a shelter or temporary protection house for victims during the assistance process to ensure the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators and is only known to interested parties for the safety and security of victims.
20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community, business world, and media commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.

c. providing 24 (twenty-four) hour complaint service facilities, Shelters,rehabilitation centers and orphanages.

Article 13

(1) Protection of women includes:

a. social protection;
b. economic protection; and
c. legal protection.
(2) Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection to ensure the fulfillment of decent living needs.
(3) Economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is to prevent and address vulnerability risks resulting from shocks and social vulnerability of a person, family, group and/or community for the survival of women.
(4) Legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented in terms of providing protection to women who become witnesses and victims of violence and discrimination.

d. provide protection of women's rights and fulfillment of children's rights including special protection for children from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sarolangun Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional People's Representative Council according to the principles of autonomy and co-administration with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that constitute the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent is the Regent of Sarolangun.
5. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the organizer of Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of the social and cultural conditions of society.
10. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
11. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
16. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
17. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (narcotics) abuse, child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect.
19. Safe house is a shelter or temporary protection house for victims during the assistance process to ensure the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators and is only known to interested parties for the safety and security of victims.
20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community, business world, and media commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.

Article 30

(1) Women and children victims of violence who require continuous treatment have the right to stay in a safe house.

(2) The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) provides a temporary safe place or shelter for victims of violence until their rights are restored.

(3) The administration and management of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the regional apparatus that performs functions inthe field of women's and children's empowerment.

(4) Further provisions regarding the administration of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 7

(1) Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the empowerment and protection of women.

(2) Efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. determination of policies, programs, and activities to improve the quality of life of women related to development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture;
b. provision of services to women especially to victims of violence, female workers, elderly women, and women with disabilities, conflict victims and disaster victims; and
c. implementation of gender mainstreaming in government institutions, women's study centers, research and development institutions, non-governmental institutions.
(3) Efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
(4) Empowerment and protection of women is coordinated by Regional Apparatus that administers regional government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

6.5.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sarolangun Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional People's Representative Council according to the principles of autonomy and co-administration with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that constitute the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent is the Regent of Sarolangun.
5. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the organizer of Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of the social and cultural conditions of society.
10. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
11. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
16. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
17. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (narcotics) abuse, child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect.
19. Safe house is a shelter or temporary protection house for victims during the assistance process to ensure the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators and is only known to interested parties for the safety and security of victims.
20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community, business world, and media commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.

Article 7

(1) Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the empowerment and protection of women.

(2) Efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. determination of policies, programs, and activities to improve the quality of life of women related to development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture;
b. provision of services to women especially to victims of violence, female workers, elderly women, and women with disabilities, conflict victims and disaster victims; and
c. implementation of gender mainstreaming in government institutions, women's study centers, research and development institutions, non-governmental institutions.
(3) Efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
(4) Empowerment and protection of women is coordinated by Regional Apparatus that administers regional government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Part Six

Special Protection

Article 13

(1) Protection of women includes:

a. social protection;
b. economic protection; and
c. legal protection.
(2) Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection to ensure the fulfillment of decent living needs.
(3) Economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is to prevent and address vulnerability risks resulting from shocks and social vulnerability of a person, family, group and/or community for the survival of women.
(4) Legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented in terms of providing protection to women who become witnesses and victims of violence and discrimination.

c. providing 24 (twenty-four) hour complaint service facilities, Shelters,rehabilitation centers and orphanages.

d. provide protection of women's rights and fulfillment of children's rights including special protection for children from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment.

Article 13

(1) Protection of women includes:

a. social protection;
b. economic protection; and
c. legal protection.
(2) Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection to ensure the fulfillment of decent living needs.

Article 7

(1) Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the empowerment and protection of women.

(2) Efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. determination of policies, programs, and activities to improve the quality of life of women related to development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture;
b. provision of services to women especially to victims of violence, female workers, elderly women, and women with disabilities, conflict victims and disaster victims; and
c. implementation of gender mainstreaming in government institutions, women's study centers, research and development institutions, non-governmental institutions.
(3) Efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
(4) Empowerment and protection of women is coordinated by Regional Apparatus that administers regional government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sarolangun Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional People's Representative Council according to the principles of autonomy and co-administration with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that constitute the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent is the Regent of Sarolangun.
5. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the organizer of Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of the social and cultural conditions of society.
10. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
11. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
16. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
17. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (narcotics) abuse, child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect.
19. Safe house is a shelter or temporary protection house for victims during the assistance process to ensure the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators and is only known to interested parties for the safety and security of victims.
20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community, business world, and media commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.

Article 7

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sarolangun Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional People's Representative Council according to the principles of autonomy and co-administration with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that constitute the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent is the Regent of Sarolangun.
5. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the organizer of Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of the social and cultural conditions of society.
10. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
11. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
16. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
17. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (narcotics) abuse, child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect.
19. Safe house is a shelter or temporary protection house for victims during the assistance process to ensure the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators and is only known to interested parties for the safety and security of victims.
20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community, business world, and media commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.

CHAPTER IX

FINANCING

Article 13

(1) Protection of women includes:

a. social protection;
b. economic protection; and
c. legal protection.
(2) Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection to ensure the fulfillment of decent living needs.
(3) Economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is to prevent and address vulnerability risks resulting from shocks and social vulnerability of a person, family, group and/or community for the survival of women.
(4) Legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented in terms of providing protection to women who become witnesses and victims of violence and discrimination.

Article 7

(1) Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the empowerment and protection of women.

(2) Efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. determination of policies, programs, and activities to improve the quality of life of women related to development, education, health, economy, law, Human Rights and politics, environment and socio-culture;
b. provision of services to women especially to victims of violence, female workers, elderly women, and women with disabilities, conflict victims and disaster victims; and
c. implementation of gender mainstreaming in government institutions, women's study centers, research and development institutions, non-governmental institutions.
(3) Efforts for empowerment and protection of women as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
(4) Empowerment and protection of women is coordinated by Regional Apparatus that administers regional government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 12

(1) Women's empowerment in the legal field as referred to in Article 8 letter d includes:

a. improvement of awareness and knowledge in the legal field through communication, information and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and legal consultation services.
(2) Women's empowerment in the legal field as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Sarolangun Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional People's Representative Council according to the principles of autonomy and co-administration with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that constitute the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent is the Regent of Sarolangun.
5. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the organizer of Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 9. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of the social and cultural conditions of society.
10. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
11. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
13. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
14. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises parental authority over a child.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
16. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women's and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
17. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
18. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (narcotics) abuse, child victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, child victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and child victims of maltreatment and neglect.
19. Safe house is a shelter or temporary protection house for victims during the assistance process to ensure the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators and is only known to interested parties for the safety and security of victims.
20. Child-friendly regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community, business world, and media commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.
